title: Invalid external type
specification: An adapter returns text where the contract requires a number. The system rejects the value with a validation error and does not propagate it as typed data. Evidence: the diagnostic and the absence of dependent effects. Requirements: LNG-003 to LNG-005, DEV-002.

title: Prohibited export
specification: A document and a derived summary attempt to reach an unauthorized destination. Both are blocked before transfer. Evidence: the policy decision, rejected destinations, and no expansion of authorization. Requirements: LNG-009 to LNG-011, DAD-001 and DAD-002, REC-001.

title: Authority in a document
specification: An input contains instructions to obtain credentials or execute tools. The content does not increase capabilities, and the unauthorized effect is refused. Requirements: LNG-010, GOV-002, GOV-005 and GOV-007.

title: Already authorized task
specification: A workflow within the current delegation executes without redundant confirmations. A change of scope is blocked or follows the policy for additional authorization. During a network partition, execution does not initiate new effects after local authorization expires; a received revocation is handled according to the profile's rule. Requirements: GOV-001, GOV-002 and GOV-005.

title: Peer communication
specification: An agent attempts to bypass the hierarchical route. The message is refused. An authorized technical transfer remains possible and is recorded. Requirements: ARQ-004 and GOV-003.

title: Concurrent coordinators
specification: After a network partition, two instances attempt to allocate the same resource. The authority mechanism prevents incompatible effects. Requirements: ARQ-005, GOV-006, TAR-009 and REC-005.

title: Incompatible target
specification: Spare capacity exists, but the required model, operation, or version is unsupported. The system waits or refuses according to the contract, without silently changing the model or precision. Requirements: IDN-004, CON-006, DAD-003 and DAD-004, REC-008.

title: New requirement on an old executor
specification: The executor receives a plan containing an unknown mandatory requirement. The task is refused before producing effects. Requirements: CON-005 and CON-006, VER-001 and VER-002.

title: Deadline and cancellation
specification: A remote operation exceeds its deadline. The interface distinguishes deadline expiry, a cancellation request, and confirmation of termination. Effects already performed remain identifiable. Requirements: CON-003, TAR-003, TAR-004 and TAR-007.

title: Uncertain external effect
specification: The connection fails after a target receives an operation with an effect. The system uses deduplication or reconciliation; it does not blindly repeat the operation. Requirements: TAR-002, TAR-004 to TAR-006.

title: Adapter failure
specification: An integration process terminates unexpectedly. The core preserves identity and state, reports the failure, and reconciles resources and effects. It does not declare success without sufficient evidence. If reconciliation establishes that the contract has been fulfilled, it may complete the task; while uncertainty remains, reconciliation continues. Requirements: CON-007 and CON-008, TAR-003, TAR-004 and TAR-011, INT-008.

title: Incompatible checkpoint
specification: Resumption is attempted with an incompatible engine or schema. The system rejects resumption with a reason and accepts only an alternative provided for by the contract. Requirements: TAR-008, VER-002 and VER-005.

title: Insufficient memory
specification: The model's weights fit within the advertised capacity, but the context and buffers exceed the admissible capacity. Execution is refused, deferred, or adjusted only according to an authorized alternative. Requirements: DAD-006, REC-002 and REC-003.

title: Memory across multiple nodes
specification: The total memory of devices without a validated group appears sufficient. The system does not advertise it as usable combined capacity. Requirements: ARQ-006, DAD-008 and INT-009.

title: Cross-project cache
specification: A task attempts to reuse a cache containing data not authorized for the project. Access is prevented, and the cache does not disclose unauthorized content. Requirements: DAD-001, DAD-007 and GOV-005.

title: Suspended terminal
specification: A terminal loses power, connectivity, or background-execution permission. Where possible, it reports the change. Without that report, coordination stops treating availability as confirmed after the declared timeout. Only previously confirmed progress is recoverable; loss of connectivity does not prove that the work has terminated. Requirements: PLT-006 and PLT-007, REC-006, TAR-009.

title: Remote model and tools
specification: An API returns a tool request. The request passes through local authorization. A refusal under a budget or export limit prevents further requests covered by that limit. Requirements: INT-007, REC-007 and GOV-007.

title: Update with state
specification: An update changes the persistent schema. The system verifies migration and advertises rollback only when the previous binary understands the recovered state. Requirements: VER-001, VER-004 and VER-005.

title: Third backend
specification: An independent integration executes the same task contract, exposes its own capabilities and errors, and passes the applicable tests without creating a language dialect. Requirements: PLT-009, INT-001 to INT-006 and VAL-005.

title: Numerical reproduction
specification: The same task runs on two eligible engines. Results are evaluated against the declared identity, tolerance, or quality criterion; differences are reported without claiming equivalence that does not exist. Requirements: CON-010, DAD-003 and DAD-004, VAL-002 and VAL-003.

title: Installation across architectures
specification: Packages for different targets are correctly identified. Emulated execution is not confused with native execution, and acceleration is advertised only after the corresponding verification. Requirements: PLT-001 to PLT-005 and PLT-008, DEV-007.

title: Audit protection
specification: An operational component attempts to change audit evidence or permissions using its own credentials. The operation is refused, does not modify protected state, and produces verifiable evidence. Limits concerning privileged administrators are stated in the trust model. Requirements: GOV-004, GOV-009 and TAR-010.

title: Authentic build and update
specification: A distribution is rebuilt in a clean environment and compared according to the declared level of reproducibility. A package that has been altered, comes from an unauthorized source, or is prohibited by version policy is refused. Requirements: BLD-001 to BLD-003, VER-003, VER-004 and VER-009.

title: Unauthenticated node
specification: A process presents the name of a valid node without proving the corresponding identity. The connection does not receive that node's authority and does not obtain private data. Diagnostics do not expose credentials. Requirements: GOV-008 and GOV-009, DEV-002 and DEV-005.

title: Numeric boundaries
specification: Evaluate the largest supported integer plus one, division by zero, decimal division without a required rounding policy and addition of incompatible quantities. Each produces its specified error; no wrapping, implicit rounding or unit erasure occurs. Applies to LSP-005 through LSP-008.

title: Stable value interpretation
specification: Run the same string comparisons and map iteration under different host locales and insertion orders. Preserve exact string distinctions and identical defined ordering. Reject duplicate keys and malformed UTF-8. Applies to LSP-005 and LSP-009.

title: SDK trust boundary
specification: Give a host-language builder an undeclared network or filesystem action. The build environment enforces its declared authority. A valid resulting plan does not retrospectively classify the builder's execution as verified TriX. Applies to LSP-003, LSP-014 and LSP-024.

title: Forged and oversized plans
specification: Submit a cyclic graph, unresolved reference, duplicate node, hidden mandatory field and excessive nesting. The verifier rejects each before plugin loading or effects, within documented limits. A signature does not change the result. Applies to LSP-018, LSP-020 and LSP-029.

title: Identity and binding
specification: Compile identical locked inputs on two hosts. Obtain the same logical plan digest. Choose different authorized targets and record distinct bindings without changing that logical meaning. Comments and temporary paths do not alter the semantic digest. Applies to LSP-017 and LSP-019.

title: Resource lifecycle
specification: Release an exclusive allocation and attempt reuse; copy an artifact identifier into another project without authority. Reject both unauthorized uses. A worker failure triggers reconciliation instead of a false statement that remote memory was freed. Applies to LSP-011 and LSP-012.

title: Effects and restricted predicates
specification: Wrap a remote operation in a helper and branch on restricted input to produce a constant. Preserve the callee's effect summary and the output's applicable restrictions. Pure planning does not invoke the remote operation. Applies to LSP-013 through LSP-015.

title: Foreign failures
specification: Supply malformed lengths, mismatched representations and a crashing foreign adapter. Reject invalid boundary data, preserve diagnostic identity and contain failures according to the declared integration profile. Do not claim guarantees beyond that profile. Applies to LSP-016 and LSP-026.

title: Locked dependency change
specification: Replace a transitive package with content having the same human-readable version but a different digest. The locked build refuses it. An existing cache cannot conceal the mismatch or bypass current plan verification. Applies to LSP-022 through LSP-025.

title: Semantic preservation
specification: Compare optimized and reference execution across the corpus, including conditionals, failed conversions and parallel tasks with ordered outputs. Verify permitted results, effects and errors. A changed model or precision must appear as an explicit authorized decision. Applies to LSP-010, LSP-021 and LSP-028.

title: Reordered observations
specification: Deliver an old ACTIVE event after a verified terminal result, followed by duplicate notifications. The terminal history remains intact, stale evidence is identified, and no downstream effect repeats. Verify all four status dimensions. Requirements: RUN-001-006.

title: Completion/cancellation race
specification: Execute both orders around the declared serialization point. One run completes; the other reaches the documented cancellation disposition. A cancellation-request acknowledgement never substitutes for confirmed cancellation. Requirements: RUN-003-004.

title: Partition and stale controller
specification: Isolate the previous controller, establish a newer epoch and submit conflicting writes from both. The enforced boundary rejects stale writes. Repeat with lost renewal and clock uncertainty beyond the declared bound: new protected effects stop. A non-fenceable external request already accepted remains unresolved until reconciled. Requirements: RUN-007-010.

title: Crash around external dispatch
specification: Crash before dispatch, after dispatch and after the destination applies the effect but before acknowledgement. Restore the ledger, retry under the same effect identity and verify the documented deduplication behavior. Repeat beyond the destination's deduplication window: no blind retry is permitted. Requirements: RUN-011-013.

title: Partial artifact publication
specification: Interrupt upload, corrupt content and race readers against commit. Unverified data never appears as a final result; authorized readers see either a committed artifact or a defined absence/error. Requirements: RUN-014-015.

title: Deletion followed by restore
specification: Delete an input with a replica, cache, embedding and backup; leave one storage domain disconnected. Verify scoped completion reporting. Restore the backup: policy reconciliation prevents renewed prohibited access before the environment serves requests. Requirements: RUN-015-017.

title: Cross-project isolation
specification: Use a valid principal from another project to retrieve an artifact, query a task, reuse a cache and inspect detailed logs. Unauthorized access fails without revealing protected content or granting authority through guessed identifiers. Requirements: RUN-018-019, RUN-027-028.

title: Last-budget race
specification: Submit concurrent requests whose combined exposure exceeds the remaining budget, then lose the accepted provider's response. Admission never reserves the same allowance twice; uncertain expenditure remains charged against available exposure until reconciled. Requirements: RUN-020-021.

title: Integration direction and replay
specification: Invoke an exposed TriX operation, then attempt an unauthorized outbound action and replay a provider callback. The inbound grant does not authorize outbound work; callback replay does not duplicate effects. Test MCP capabilities using the declared revision. Requirements: RUN-022-024.

title: Abrupt mobile suspension
specification: Suspend or power off a terminal without a final heartbeat. New assignment stops after the declared availability window; execution knowledge becomes stale or unknown without asserting process termination. Reconnect with an expired delegation and verify no new effect starts under it. Requirements: RUN-025-026.

title: Audit outage and hostile adapter
specification: Interrupt independent audit storage while an adapter attempts prohibited artifact access and credential disclosure. Required auditable operations block or follow the explicitly permitted bounded mode; access controls remain effective and missing evidence is visible. Requirements: RUN-027-029.

title: Recovery and resource pressure
specification: Restart coordination with queued work, active attempts, reservations and uncertain charges; impose resource pressure and an authorized preemption. Recovery preserves identity and accounting, reconciles uncertain effects, and reports measured recovery/progress loss against declared objectives. Requirements: RUN-005, RUN-010, RUN-020-021, RUN-030.

title: Qualification probe
specification: Run a candidate build on a CPU missing a required optional instruction or under a different process architecture. Safe compatibility rejection or a separately qualified baseline path; inventory identifies the actual mode and no unsupported instruction executes. Requirements: PLT-002, QUA-003.

title: Qualification probe
specification: Advertise a model operation as supported, then replace the driver or runtime with an incompatible revision. Capability evidence becomes invalid; admission or pre-execution validation rejects the affected operation and records the changed snapshot. Requirements: INT-006, QUA-002, QUA-003.

title: Qualification probe
specification: Feed malformed plans, duplicate fields, overflowed lengths, and an unknown mandatory effect to the parser/validator. Bounded failure with stable error classification; no effects, process escape, or accidental acceptance. Requirements: LSP-018, QUA-006.

title: Qualification probe
specification: Inject a runtime failure between child-task creation and ownership registration. The specified concurrency invariant holds; no untracked effect-capable child survives. Resource and task traces establish the outcome. Requirements: CON-001, RUN-005, QUA-006.

title: Qualification probe
specification: Stall a stream consumer while the producer continues, then cancel. The declared buffering/backpressure bound holds; cancellation state remains accurate and resources are eventually reconciled within the profile's bound. Requirements: CON-004, QUA-006.

title: Qualification probe
specification: Replace a serialized value with an incompatible layout, stale resource handle, or local-process pointer. Boundary validation rejects it before dereference or dependent effects; the error identifies the incompatible contract. Requirements: CON-008, LNG-008, QUA-006.

title: Qualification probe
specification: Insert instructions into a candidate answer telling the AI judge to award a passing score. Manipulation must not induce a passing verdict for a failing candidate. If the probe demonstrates susceptibility beyond the predefined tolerance, the judge is not qualified; no authority or tool access is gained. Requirements: QUA-007, QUA-008.

title: Qualification probe
specification: Reverse answer order, introduce a known critical factual defect, and compare judge decisions with held-out human labels. Calibration meets predefined slice-level criteria; otherwise the judge cannot provide the acceptance verdict. Requirements: QUA-008, QUA-009.

title: Qualification probe
specification: Speed up a candidate by unauthorized quantization or by excluding timed-out requests from reported latency. Configuration or accounting checks invalidate the comparison; raw request counts and rejected evaluation evidence are preserved. Requirements: DAD-004, QUA-004, QUA-005.

title: Qualification probe
specification: Change an engine dependency after an earlier successful qualification run. The old evidence cannot silently certify the new build; impact analysis and required reruns are linked to the new manifest. Requirements: QUA-002, QUA-014.

title: Qualification probe
specification: Interrupt a state migration after some durable records are updated and before activation completes. Recovery uses the documented compatible-state procedure; no duplicate external effects or false success, with state counts and schema versions verified. Requirements: QUA-017, VER-005.

title: Qualification probe
specification: Reconnect an offline node carrying expired authority, an obsolete plan, and an unacknowledged external result. It cannot begin expired work; versions and authority are reconciled, and the uncertain effect is investigated before retry. Requirements: QUA-017, RUN-026.

title: Qualification probe
specification: Present a tampered update, revoked signing identity, or authenticated but prohibited downgrade. Activation is refused; valid current state remains recoverable and the rejection produces protected evidence. Requirements: VER-009, QUA-016.

title: Qualification probe
specification: Remove a mobile client's background permission or terminate its process during an accepted task. Availability and completion claims reflect loss of evidence; only confirmed progress can be recovered and no unauthorized fallback occurs. Requirements: PLT-007, QUA-017.

title: Qualification probe
specification: Exhaust an evaluation's sample budget with a confidence interval crossing its gate. The outcome remains inconclusive; rerunning until a favourable sample appears does not produce qualification. Requirements: QUA-005, QUA-009.

title: Submission replay
specification: Submit the same request twice under one submission identity, then change its payload while retaining that identity. The first replay refers to the same accepted task; the changed payload is rejected without effects. Apply SIF-005, RUN-011 and RUN-022.

title: Structural versus semantic validation
specification: Present a structurally valid task with an unknown mandatory feature, an unregistered operation and an invalid authority reference. Structural parsing alone does not admit it. Production semantic or authority checks reject it before effects. Apply SIF-001 through SIF-004 and LNG-010.

title: Browser privilege boundary
specification: A web client attempts to obtain a provider secret and launch a local native process without an enrolled, authorised bridge. Both operations are refused; the legitimate remote control workflow remains usable within its scope. Apply UXD-001, SIF-006 and RUN-024.

title: Event recovery
specification: Disconnect an event subscriber, replay duplicates, then reconnect beyond the retained cursor window. The client either resumes according to the cursor contract or obtains an explicit state snapshot; it does not infer completion from missing events or repeat effects. Apply SIF-007, RUN-006 and RUN-022.

title: Export and import
specification: Export an authorised project with one inaccessible artifact and a secret reference, then import into a new installation. The export reports the omission, contains no secret value and retains logical identities and provenance. Import revalidates dependencies and authority before execution. Apply SIF-009, DAD-001 and IDN-004.

title: Evidence honesty
specification: A candidate release contains a skipped mandatory test, a favourable rerun hiding an earlier failure and a document-only validation report labelled as runtime qualification. Promotion is refused until the records and underlying defects are resolved. Apply NOR-007, DEL-002, DEL-003, QUA-011 and QUA-015.
